title: stochastic-latency-cost-crosstab-proto
content:
Purpose:
This is a working proto for a compact crosstab-style benchmark report that compares latency and cost across a set of realistic request mixes and scheduling knobs. Goal is: quick, skimmable collateral we can drop into the Console help UI and the sales one-pager. Draft is intentionally terse and contains raw ASCII charts + tables for rapid iteration.

Scope / TL;DR:
- Models: open-llm-13B (fp16), open-llm-70B (q4_0), distilled-7B (int8)
- Hardware: A100-80GB, H100-80GB (single-GPU serving units)
- Workloads: interactive-chat (median 40 tokens/resp), long-prompt-chat (median 400 tokens), embedding-batch (batch size 64 embeddings)
- Knobs compared: small-window-batch (50ms wait), opportunistic-fill (no-wait, best-effort pack), prefetch-kv (context prefetch enabled)
- Metrics: p50/p90/p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec throughput, $/k token (approx infra amortized + GPU time only)

Experiment notes (quick):
- Runs executed from internal cluster during low-noise window (2029-07-18 thru 2029-07-22). 5 repeats per cell, report shows median of medians.
- Included cold-start penalty rows where worker spin-up happened (cold penalty = additional 120ms median for first 5 requests). Cold rows flagged.
- Synthetic client used realistic pacing: Poisson arrivals matching observed customer session traces (sample set: session-trace-v2).

Compact crosstab (interactive-chat, median 40 tokens):
Mode, Model, HW, p50(ms), p90(ms), p99(ms), tokens/s, $/k tok
small-window-batch, open-llm-13B, A100, 42, 120, 420, 180, $0.45
opportunistic-fill, open-llm-13B, A100, 36, 110, 500, 150, $0.52
prefetch-kv, open-llm-13B, A100, 40, 115, 410, 185, $0.47
small-window-batch, open-llm-70B, H100, 55, 160, 620, 210, $0.78
opportunistic-fill, open-llm-70B, H100, 48, 150, 700, 180, $0.89
prefetch-kv, open-llm-70B, H100, 52, 155, 600, 220, $0.80

Observations (interactive-chat):
- Small-window-batch gives best p50 and tokens/sec for 13B on A100; however p99 is higher under opportunistic packing due to head-of-line mixing and jitter.
- For larger models on H100, prefetch-kv recovers tokens/sec while keeping p99 slightly better than opportunistic-fill.
- $/k token is sensitive to packing efficiency: opportunistic-fill sometimes looks cheaper at p50 but worsens p99 (poor for latency SLOs).

Compact crosstab (long-prompt-chat, median 400 tokens):
Mode, Model, HW, p50(ms), p90(ms), p99(ms), tokens/s, $/k tok
small-window-batch, open-llm-13B, A100, 720, 1100, 2300, 22, $1.65
opportunistic-fill, open-llm-13B, A100, 680, 1250, 4100, 18, $1.56
prefetch-kv, open-llm-13B, A100, 690, 1080, 2200, 24, $1.60
small-window-batch, open-llm-70B, H100, 450, 900, 1800, 30, $2.20
opportunistic-fill, open-llm-70B, H100, 420, 980, 3200, 26, $2.05
prefetch-kv, open-llm-70B, H100, 430, 880, 1700, 33, $2.12

Observations (long-prompt):
- Prefetch-kv shines for long prompts: it reduces large p99 spikes by avoiding repeated KV recomputation across turns.
- Small-window-batch has marginally better median for 70B on H100 due to steadier utilization.
- Opportunistic-fill reduces raw $/k on a per-GPU-hour basis but creates multi-second tail events (bad for UI-facing SLAs).

Embedding-batch (batch size 64):
Mode, Model, HW, p50(ms) per batch, throughput (emb/s), $/k emb
batch-only, distilled-7B, A100, 110, 5800, $0.06
async-pack, distilled-7B, A100, 95, 6400, $0.05
striped-prefetch, distilled-7B, A100, 100, 6100, $0.055

Observations (embeddings):
- Large synchronous batches are best for stable $/emb. Opportunistic async packing gives small wins in throughput with lower median latency.
- For embedding workloads, network serialization overhead dominates once GPU is saturated; codec improvements matter.

ASCII charts (latency vs cost sketch, interactive-chat 13B A100):
Cost ($/k tok) 0.4 |#######-------| 0.6
P90 latency (ms)   80   |#######---    | 160
P99 latency (ms)  200   |#########-----| 700
(Chart is qualitative: left-hand region = low-cost low-latency, right-hand region = expensive / long tails)

Sensitivity notes (quick bullets):
- Cold-start frequency: every 300s TTL yields measurable p99 inflation; prewarm policy reduces cold-induced p99 by ~90ms median.
- Sessionized affinity: pinning session to worker reduces p90/p99 for long-prompt-chat but raises $/k by ~6% due to lower bin-packing between sessions.
- Quantization regime: q4_0 for 70B reduces $/k by ~17% vs fp16 but increases p99 jitter under opportunistic-fill by ~12% (kernel variability).

Recommended messaging for Console one-pager (short bullets):
- "Pick small-window-batch for predictable UI latency; use prefetch-kv when context lengths are high."
- "Opportunistic packing can lower per-token cost but increases tail risk — recommended for background/async workloads (embeddings, batch-generation)."
- "Quantization is cost-effective for throughput-heavy workloads; validate tail behavior on your prompt mix."

Open questions / next experiments:
- Run long-tail (p99.99) probes with real customer session traces to measure probability of multi-second tail under opportunistic-fill.
- Evaluate lightweight codec (msgpack v2) to reduce serialization overhead for embeddings + small responses.
- Cost model: integrate infra amortization + rack-level amortization to update $/k numbers (current values only include GPU amortized time).

Where this draft lives and how to iterate:
- Drop feedback in thread #console-perf (Slack) or add inline comments in linked GitHub PR.
- If we're happy with direction, turn this proto into a 1-page sales-facing PDF + a Console explainer card.

Notes to self (todo):
- Add simple histogram ASCII export for p50/p90/p99 across 1000 samples per cell.
- Attach raw CSVs to the GitHub PR.
__notes: working-doc: informal, contains shorthand and unresolved todos. Keep in Drive for iteration.
